name: espeak-ng-699e7969-blind28
instr:
# Diagnosing a multilingual text-to-audio library without a test suite

The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits.

An application built on this library turns written material into audio, and it now gets that wrong from the moment it is brought up to the audio that finally comes out. Bringing it up in the mode that sends audio straight to the playback hardware and then asking it to say a sentence produces nothing audible and fails instead. Asking it in the plain way to say a buffer of text comes back with an audio failure status even though the call ran all the way to the end. Closing the library down when the run is over crashes rather than returning. Handing it a wide-character buffer to say drops the final unit, so what it works from is one short. Handing it text labelled with a character set it has no reader for no longer reports that the character set is unknown; the call runs on and crashes.

Driving the same work from a terminal, the switch that names a file to take the input from is ignored: the name written after it is thrown away and nothing in that file is ever read.

Input that carries mark-up goes wrong in several ways. A tag part way through asking for a different rate leaves the pace as it was: what follows is neither given the duration the tag asked for nor produced at the speed it asked for.
